issues.legal_issue: Tax recovery proceedings may proceed against a receiver holding the relevant assets when that receiver was assessed for the income giving rise to the tax debt.
material_facts: Tax assessments for income earned by the firm were made on one of its receivers, including for the years whose unpaid taxes were at issue.
After other receivers had held the assets, the assessed receiver was appointed again as receiver of those assets.
The tax authority sought permission to proceed against him in his capacity as receiver.
issues.conclusion: The appeals were allowed, and the tax authority was permitted to proceed against the assessed receiver as receiver of the firm’s assets.
issues.legal_principle: The court resolved the appeals on the fact that the receiver then holding the assets was himself an assessee under the relevant assessments, so no question of substituting a later, unassessed receiver arose. Although section 41(2) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, was the certified point of appeal, the court found it unnecessary to interpret that provision. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.tax_recovery_appeal: A tax authority appeals the refusal of permission to pursue recovery from assets held by a receiver.
predicates.receiver_holds_relevant_assets: The person against whom recovery is sought currently holds the relevant assets as receiver.
predicates.receiver_was_assessed_for_tax: The receiver currently holding the assets was assessed for the tax debt arising from the relevant income.

issues.definition: When a tax-recovery appeal concerns assets currently held by a receiver who was assessed for the relevant tax debt, recovery is permitted against that receiver.
